messages.content:
Here is the trip. It is everything you get.

Shape: city-and-culture
Leaving from: Toronto
Going to: Rome
Dates: 2027-10-09 to 2027-10-16, fixed
Travellers: 2
Ages that change the plan: 68, 71
Access needs: One of us can walk a few kilometres a day but not on cobbles for long, and stairs without a handrail are difficult.
Budget: 350 CAD, per-day
Appetite for effort: gentle
Roughest night they will accept: hotel
Would rule the trip out: Nothing that needs to be at a place before 09:00, No guided group tours

About this city-and-culture:
Pace: slow
Interests: Roman archaeology, Baroque painting, markets
In their words: We have been to Rome once, thirty years ago, and saw the obvious things then. We would rather spend a whole morning in one place than see four.

candidates.title: Galleria Borghese reservation for Baroque painting
candidates.summary: Strong Baroque painting collection in a manageable number of rooms, suited to a slow, single-site morning. Entry is usually by timed reservation, but I have not checked current availability, opening days or the lead time, so those are left blank. Confirm the lift or ramp arrangements if stairs are a concern.

candidates.title: Roman Forum and Palatine Hill combined ticket
candidates.summary: Covers the core of Roman archaeology in one ticket. The ground is uneven, with slopes and steps and some stretches of old paving, so check the access notes against your walking and stairs limits before committing. I have not verified current prices or whether the combined ticket still applies.

candidatesAccepted.title: Hotel Raphael near Piazza Navona
candidatesAccepted.summary: A quiet, established hotel a short walk from Piazza Navona and the Baroque churches with Caravaggio and Bernini works, so mornings can stay on one site. I have not checked lift access or step-free routes, and the nearby streets are cobbled, so confirm both before booking.

candidatesAccepted.title: Hotel Duca d'Alba near the Colosseum
candidatesAccepted.summary: A small hotel close to the Colosseum and the Roman Forum, which suits a slow morning at one archaeological site without long transfers. I could not confirm whether it has a lift or a handrail on its stairs, and the surrounding streets are cobbled, so ask about both before booking.

candidatesAccepted.title: Hotel Campo de' Fiori area
candidatesAccepted.summary: A central hotel near the Campo de' Fiori market, which suits the market interest and keeps the Baroque centre within walking distance. I do not know its access features or whether the walk from the piazza is step-free, so check both; the area is cobbled and lively in the mornings.

candidatesAccepted.title: Galleria Borghese paintings
candidatesAccepted.summary: Baroque painting at an unhurried pace, with Caravaggio and Bernini sculpture in one villa. Timed entry is usually required, which I have not checked, so confirm booking before relying on it. Mostly flat, with some stairs to check.

candidatesAccepted.title: Capitoline Museums, a long morning
candidatesAccepted.summary: Roman archaeology and Baroque painting, including Caravaggio, in one large collection. I did not check opening hours or the length of the galleries, so the duration is a guess and the walk between halls may be longer than expected.

candidatesAccepted.title: Roman Forum and Palatine Hill
candidatesAccepted.summary: Roman archaeology at the centre of ancient Rome, seen slowly. The site has uneven ancient paving and slopes, and some steps without handrails, so only the walker who can manage a few kilometres on rough ground should attempt the full loop. I did not check opening hours.

candidatesAccepted.title: Palazzo Massimo Roman sculpture
candidatesAccepted.summary: Roman archaeology indoors, with mosaics and sculpture on level floors, which suits sore feet and the cobble limit. I did not check hours or whether timed entry applies.

place.name: Museo Nazionale Romano, Palazzo Massimo alle Terme

candidatesAccepted.title: Palazzo Barberini Baroque rooms
candidatesAccepted.summary: Baroque painting and a ceiling fresco by Pietro da Cortona, in a palace that is easy to take slowly. Opening times and the number of stairs are not known to me.

candidatesAccepted.title: Campo de' Fiori morning market
candidatesAccepted.summary: A working market for slow looking, food and small purchases, with a few cafés for sitting. I do not know how busy it is at a given hour or how long a visit takes, so the duration is left unknown.

candidatesAccepted.title: Testaccio market and food hall
candidatesAccepted.summary: A neighbourhood market with food stalls, a fitting alternative to the historic markets, with fewer crowds. Paving and walking distance are unchecked, and I do not know opening hours.

candidatesAccepted.title: Doria Pamphilj gallery
candidatesAccepted.summary: Baroque painting in a private palace, including Velázquez's portrait of Innocent X. Opening days and hours are not known to me, so check before going.

candidatesAccepted.title: Campo de' Fiori morning market
candidatesAccepted.summary: A working market in a square that has been feeding Romans for centuries, good for slow looking at produce and a seated snack. The square is cobbled, so pick a bench or café edge rather than walking its length; I could not check how busy it is at different hours, so the time it takes is unknown.

candidatesAccepted.title: Mercato Trionfale covered food market
candidatesAccepted.summary: A large covered market north of the Vatican with mostly level indoor aisles, a gentler alternative to open-air cobbles and a good place to see what Romans actually buy. I have not confirmed its current opening days, and it is generally closed on Sundays, so check before going; the time you would spend there is unmeasured.

candidatesAccepted.title: Antico Forno Roscioli bakery stop
candidatesAccepted.summary: A long-running bakery near Campo de' Fiori known for pizza bianca and filled rolls, a simple sit-or-take-away stop that suits a gentle pace. I did not verify its current hours or whether it takes reservations for seating, so those are unknown to me.

candidatesAccepted.title: Sant'Eustachio Il Caffè coffee break
candidatesAccepted.summary: A well-known espresso bar near the Pantheon where the coffee is served with a classic sugar-heavy method; standing at the bar costs less than sitting. It has no stairs to manage, and I could not confirm current seating or hours.
